open_points.question: Which named component is the data provider, who authors or generates `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`, and from what authoritative input does it mint each OwnerFormField value?
options: The specification compiler generates the provider constant from a declared specification source.
A named hand-maintained provider module authors the constant directly.
Another release-building component generates the constant from an external source.
open_points.default_guess: A named data-provider module, generated from the specification during release assembly, mints the OwnerFormField values.

witness.initial: The specification and a provider constant can be assembled into a release.
events: The specification text and the provider constant contain different facts for one field.
outcomes: The builder treats the specification as authoritative and regenerates the constant.
The builder treats the provider constant as authoritative and ships its facts.
witness.observer: The owner using the affected form and the generated request reader

open_points.question: Which generated product actions read `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`: form rendering, decoding owner form submissions, decoding owner query parameters, or all of them?
options: The form renderer and both form- and query-decoding paths read the same provider constant.
Only the decoding paths read the constant; rendering obtains field names elsewhere.
Only the renderer reads the constant; decoding obtains field names elsewhere.
open_points.default_guess: Every owner-interface path that renders, writes, or reads these fields derives its field names from the same provider constant.

witness.initial: The release contains an owner-page renderer, a form decoder, a query decoder, and `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`.
events: The owner opens a page whose action uses one of the declared fields.
The owner submits the rendered form or query.
outcomes: Both rendering and decoding read the constant, so changing a row changes both actions together.
Only decoding reads the constant while rendering uses separately embedded names, so the two actions can diverge after a release change.
witness.observer: The owner submitting the page and the Registry action receiving the request
